tests: tests/integration/context/test_memory_worker.py and test_memory_index.py: real files, real Git, the real Gateway route and the released Redis. The embedder is a deterministic stand-in there; pilot.json uses the real one.

cases.case: first file published at once and marked incomplete; open files first
edit replaces only that file; delete leaves; rename moves; a file the policy now excludes leaves
an excluded file is never read or indexed
branches, worktrees and clones never share a scope
a new caller appears without a rebuild; dirty and committed trees are published differently
a reader pinned to an epoch keeps its view; a reader cannot name a building epoch
only the building epoch can be written or published
competing workers leave one winner; a fenced-out writer changes nothing; a slow embedder keeps its lease
cancel then resume redoes at most one window
a killed worker leaves nothing visible it did not finish, and a restart completes
a file interrupted between its batches is redone whole, and a crash's leftovers are not served
a file interrupted and then deleted or excluded leaves nothing published
a retirement is written once, so an earlier published view stays as it was
after an ordinary pass prunes, a reader pinned earlier is refused with EPOCH_EXPIRED and never answered partly
a drop overtaking a read is a refusal, not an empty answer; nothing from before a drop can name the line that replaced it
a drop takes the line out of service in its first step: between batches nothing reads a part of it, and an interrupted drop accepts no writes until it is run again
a catalogue cannot name or seal an epoch the line does not have
a lease another owner took during a re-acquire is not replaced; cleanup decides from state read inside its transaction

the deadline covers execution: an expired request does not reach the store, a slow catalogue stops early, a read whose only step is slow is refused, a batch that outlasts it writes nothing, a lease or open that expires partway changes nothing more, a read that finishes late is refused, and a slow startup check counts

a further edit to an already-dirty file is not called complete, tracked or untracked, nor one that keeps its size and time; a repository Git cannot read is never complete, from its root or a folder beneath; the final check stops for a cancel and gives way to a turn
a resumed partial cold build needs the cold slot; losing the slot stops the worker; a brief outage does not end the heartbeat
a source that moves during a pass is not called complete
only one workspace cold-builds at a time
an outage pauses the worker and a later pass completes
a cursor cannot change scope; a host holding the same key reads another scope only by naming it (the stated residual)

revert_check.evidence: revert-check.json holds every guard's file digest, the one test that failed and its failure, under the rule stated there
revert_check.history: The first run left 2 survivors and 2 cases with no mutation; closing them found a reader could name an unpublished epoch. A later check that required the named test to fail showed one earlier catch was false: removing the heartbeat's start crashed an unrelated test. That case now mutates the heartbeat itself.
